tools.name: manage_avatar
tools.description: Read live AI-avatar capabilities, official avatars, saved avatars, and provider-neutral voice choices; create, revise, import, inspect, or delete an avatar; and inspect or edit avatar-video batches and attempts. Load the digital-human Skill before use. Resolve only the fields needed by the user's current intent; this is not a fixed wizard. Avatar selection is always preview-mandatory. Never ask with text-only saved-versus-official options. Read saved identities and the official catalog, then use the Widget Forms Skill's visual-choice surface for the current host. In embedded ChatCut, write each concrete ready identity only as <visual-option avatar-id="identityId"/>; the host prefers its live preview video and falls back to its preview image. In Codex, never emit raw ChatCut tags: use identityId as id, name as label, previewVideoUrl as previewVideo, and previewImageUrl as preview so it remains the poster and fallback. Official catalog results include curated tags for factual filtering and a description explaining suitable use cases. Use both to recommend among returned avatars, and never infer missing identity attributes from appearance. When the user specifies gender, age, ethnicity, or a search intent, pass the corresponding catalog filters so the backend filters the complete database-backed catalog before pagination. Keep the same filters when using a returned continuation token. For an official avatar with a returned defaultVoiceRef, first ask whether to use its official built-in voice or choose another voice, then stop and wait. If accepted, use that defaultVoiceRef. For a saved custom avatar with a returned defaultVoiceRef, use it automatically unless the user explicitly asks to change voices; do not ask them to confirm the saved default again. Call manage_voice action="list" use="avatar" only after the official-avatar user chooses another voice, when the custom-avatar user asks to change voices, or when no defaultVoiceRef exists. When an exact non-default voice must be selected, audition is mandatory: never ask with text-only voice-name pills. For that list, recommend only entries with a non-empty previewUrl through the Widget Forms Skill's playable voice-choice surface and always append a localized clone_voice action. In embedded ChatCut this is one <form-visual id="voiceRef" media-kind="audio"> with playable <visual-option/> cards and a final <visual-option value="clone_voice" name="Clone Voice"/> card; in published plugins never emit raw ChatCut tags and map voiceRef to the host option id and previewUrl to its audio URL. Photo-avatar creation requires an imported project JPEG/PNG plus explicit likeness consent. Never pass an external source URL. Delete only after explicit confirmation. Voice results expose opaque voiceRef values. Do not request, infer, or reveal the underlying provider, model, engine, or provider-specific identifiers.

tools.name: submit_avatar_video
tools.description:
Submit a final AI-avatar video generation batch and create video assets in the current project library. This tool does not create an avatar identity, choose a voice, place clips on the timeline, or export.

Load the digital-human Skill first. Call only when the user's current intent has a ready avatar and all required speech, script, aspect-ratio, resolution, and consent constraints resolved. Use the opaque defaultVoiceRef returned by manage_avatar catalog/list/get after the user accepts an official avatar's built-in voice, or automatically for a saved custom avatar unless the user explicitly asks to change voices. Otherwise use an opaque voiceRef returned by manage_voice use=avatar action=list after the user chooses another voice, or one project audio asset. ChatCut resolves the generation provider and engine; never request or expose them. For project audio, pass the original asset to this tool exactly once. Do not inspect its file extension or container, transcode it, split it with Bash or media tools, import replacement parts, or call this tool once per part. ChatCut automatically prepares over-limit audio and submits all ordered parts as one generation batch. If progress narration is useful, say only that ChatCut is splitting the long audio while preserving its complete content and order. Do not add implementation details about where or how the work runs. Pass speech as a JSON object, never as a quoted or JSON-stringified value. For example: {"type":"audio-asset","assetId":"..."} or {"type":"voice","voiceRef":"...","text":"..."}. After all slots are resolved, this tool obtains a live credit estimate and shows it in the final generation confirmation card before submitting. Never calculate or quote a hardcoded avatar-video price. The result contains batch, task, segment, and generation job IDs. Generation continues in the background and completed videos appear in the project library. Do not add a Bash sleep, call manage_avatar action=get-batch, or read status repeatedly in the same turn. If a follow-up step in this request needs the completed videos and track_progress describes action=wait as registering an automatic follow-up, call it once with the jobIds and a note, then end the turn; otherwise end the turn immediately after submission. In a later user turn, use track_progress only when the user asks for status or resumes a follow-up step that needs the completed asset. Do not quote non-terminal numeric progress to the user because it represents coarse internal stages, not a completion estimate. Use manage_avatar action=get-batch for ordered segment and attempt state.

tools.name: manage_voice
tools.description: Cloned voices currently expose no numeric speech-speed, pause-length or target-duration controls in submit_voice. Use only declared supportedControls; do not infer controls from other voices or underlying services. Text cues are not guaranteed timing controls. Use one unified voice surface for official ChatCut voices and the current user's cloned voices. For voice selection, call action="list" with voiceType="all". It returns one normalized candidate list: custom voices first, followed by filtered official voices. Build one playable audition UI from these returned tuples; never merge a static Skill catalog with a separate custom-voice lookup. Official voices support only action="list". Custom voices support list, check-create-access, apply, clone, preview, rename, and delete. Pass the returned voiceRef to submit_voice or submit_avatar_video according to supportedUses; for a custom voice, only after apply succeeds. A cloned voice name, preview text, or recency does not identify the speaker in the current source. Use sourceAssetId/sourceProjectId as provenance facts, not voice recognition. Missing provenance is unknown, never a match. Reuse for the current speaker only with a verified source association or a user selection resolved to one candidate by attached reference, ID, unique name or picker choice. A preference for saved voices alone is not a selection; ask when ambiguous. Otherwise clone the authorized current source or ask the user to select. Keep provider names and provider-specific identifiers internal. Clone only after explicit ownership/permission confirmation, and delete only after explicit permanent-delete confirmation. Custom cloning accepts a project audio asset; ChatCut Desktop also accepts a video asset and uses its complete default audio track, extracted locally without creating another project asset. The reference audio must be 10–180 seconds and at most 25 MiB; a Desktop video file itself may be larger. On Desktop, load the voice Skill before searching for submit_voice in the skill-voice tool group. If voice generation is unavailable, tell the user; do not substitute operating system speech synthesis such as macOS say.

tools.name: video_translation
tools.description: Load the video-translation Skill for ALL such requests, with or without lip-sync; it selects the route and owns review. Use this tool only for integrated provider translation, never merely to transcribe or review independent dubbing. Use list_languages, prepare, get, generate on the same taskId. Preparation and edits do not charge; supplier draft cost unverified. prepare never renders; get is read-only. Both lip-sync choices require review. Show editable source-language text by default; target review is optional. Users need not know the target language. Apply source corrections to the target draft and save both SRTs on the same revision. Show connected readable text; keep cue timing internally. The provider does not retranslate source corrections; never render an unsaved preview. generate requires the exact authorized revision and an explicit audioOnly: true dubs speech and keeps the picture; false also lip-syncs mouths, so do not call submit_lipsync afterward. The whole asset is processed; export ranges first. No speaker/spatial selector; time crops cannot isolate overlapping voices or protect others. Edit final target wording in the existing draft. Complete rewrites default to voice/TTS with reviewed audio and timing, then optional submit_lipsync; new presenter performances use digital-human. Voice samples are not final dialogue. Subtitle-only work is separate. On timeout get the same task before retrying. Fix content in drafts, voice in audio, mouths in lip-sync. Never repeat paid stages to fix import. Report unsupported capabilities; don't silently change treatment. At most 10 video generations run at once per account across video tools; extra submits are rejected, so wait for a running job to finish instead of retrying.

Omit to use the complete library transcript. On same-task editing, pair source corrections with updated targetTranscriptSrt. This is a ChatCut review reference, not a provider retranslation input; major new dialogue belongs in the new-script workflow.

tools.name: submit_lipsync
tools.description: Synchronize an existing video's visible speaker mouth with FINAL audio. Does not translate, clone voices, write dialogue, generate speech or create avatar performances. Changing dialogue does not authorize mouth changes: if the picture must stay unchanged, replace audio only. Load lipsync Skill. Reuse supplied final audio; otherwise generate or reuse final speech and resolve timing. Interactive Desktop asks for review of actual audio and treatment before paid rendering; external preauthorized callers must obtain approval first. Do not repeat identity/script questions for unchanged approved audio. For translation with automatic source-voice matching, default to video_translation: it includes lip-sync. A specified reusable voice or separately reviewable audio can use voice then this tool. Use one visible speaker in a suitable shot. Align speech windows, pauses and picture meaning: equal total durations do not prove alignment. Resolve duration policy first. Multi-speaker assignment, severe occlusion and arbitrary duration mismatches are not guaranteed. Export a section as a separate asset to process only that section. Returns an asynchronous job, not a quality assessment. Track it and continue the requested edit with the resulting video. Natural mouth synchronization requires continuous audiovisual inspection, not static frames, metadata or timeline placement. On uncertain responses inspect the existing job before retrying. Fix wrong words or voice in the audio first; repeated lip-sync cannot fix them. At most 10 video generations run at once per account across video tools; extra submits are rejected, so wait for a running job to finish instead of retrying.

tools.name: track_progress
tools.description: Track work in the current local Project. target=subagent uses taskIds (1 to 20 full UUIDs returned by delegate_task) and supports status or wait. status returns an immediate snapshot; wait holds this tool call until all selected tasks complete or any task pauses, fails, is interrupted or is cancelled. It returns all selected states immediately when attention is needed; other specialists keep running. Call wait once, without repeated status polling. Paused is terminal for this wait but is not success; resume the same task with concrete feedback when appropriate. Cancelling the wait does not cancel the specialists. Completed entries preserve the delivered assetId or caption template.path/runtime; result retains the original worker receipt, including available publication evidence. Caption-template tasks have no library asset: never send their taskIds as generation jobIds. Other targets accept full or unique short IDs. target=generation (default) uses jobIds and supports status, wait, params; pixel/audio effects and transitions use local specialist state and never query backend generation jobs; wait awaits that local task without cancelling it when the chat is interrupted. Other generation types wait for the detached backend job and import its output. A generation wait returns once every job completes, any job fails, or status is temporarily unavailable after bounded retries. An unavailable entry is non-terminal: its current generation state is unknown, not failed; check the same job after checkBackAfterSeconds and never resubmit just because status could not be read. Numeric generation progress is a coarse pipeline stage, not a precise provider percentage or ETA; progressNote explains missing detail; jobs still running keep running. A paused or interrupted local task is not completed; continue the same taskId with delegate_task resume rather than creating a duplicate. tools.name: manage_skill
tools.description:
Manage reusable ChatCut workflow skills.

This tool manages saved Workflow Skills, including catalog skills and user skills shared by ID. ChatCut's built-in capability playbooks (talking-head-guide, motion-graphic-gen, video-gen, ...) are a separate system and will never show up here; their absence from this list does not mean they don't exist.

A workflow skill is a user-visible reusable Claude-style skill package for the agent: goals, context, workflow steps, preferences, rules, quality checks, optional references, examples, and lightweight scripts. It is NOT a brittle tool-parameter template. Do not write low-level tool arguments into a user skill unless the user explicitly owns that stable product concept.

One durable path:
- DB is the canonical shared store.
- Sandbox files are temporary drafts or per-turn mounted packages. manage_skill does not install saved Skills into a CLI's user-level Skill directory.
- To create or update a skill from the ChatCut sandbox, write a Claude-style package there and pass sourceDirectory.
- From the ChatCut plugin (Codex / Claude Code — no ChatCut sandbox), pass the contents inline as packageFiles instead, and get returns the full package inline for the current turn.

Package shape:
- Minimum: SKILL.md at the draft root.
- Optional lightweight files: references/*, examples/*, scripts/*.
- Do not include project media asset ids, heavyweight assets, private chat dumps, credentials, or generated media.
- Total package size must stay under 1 MB.

Actions:
- list: list skills with source: "mine", "preset", or "all" (default "mine").
- fork: copy a skill by agentSkillId into your account, including its full package and display media. Returns a new independent ID; optional name overrides its name.
- get: load a skill for use. Your own and catalog skills are returned as they are; another user's shared skill is saved to your account as an independent copy, or your existing copy is reused. Returns the package, materialized to .claude/skills/<packageName>/ or inlined on connectors. Use the returned ID for later edits.
- create_from_directory: create a user skill from a sandbox package directory (sourceDirectory) or from inline contents (packageFiles).
- update_from_directory: update an owned user skill; pass sourceDirectory (defaults to the location written by get) or inline packageFiles.
- rename: update user-facing name and optional description/summary only.
- delete: delete an owned user skill.

Typical create flow:
1. Use Write/Edit to create a package such as .chatcut/skill-drafts/<slug>/SKILL.md. Add references/, examples/, or scripts/ only when useful.
2. Call manage_skill with action: "create_from_directory", sourceDirectory, and name if SKILL.md does not have a clear H1.
3. Recap what was saved and ask whether it matches the user's intended workflow.

Typical update flow:
1. Call get for the existing skill so the package lands at .claude/skills/<packageName>/.
2. Edit those files in place with Edit/Write.
3. Call update_from_directory with the same skill id; sourceDirectory is inferred.

Using skills:
- When the user provides a shared skill ID, call get directly; unlisted shared skills do not appear in list.
- Catalog skills are read-only and stay current with catalog updates. When the user wants to change one, fork it and edit the copy. Otherwise use fork only when they explicitly want an additional copy.
- If the user attached a workflow skill in the composer UI, the backend mounts it as a normal Claude skill package for this turn and tells the agent to load it with the Skill tool before editing.
- If the user asks in natural language to use a saved or preset skill, call list with the right source and get the matching skill, then follow its SKILL.md for the current turn. Do not persist it to the project.

Sharing: user skills are unlisted, but anyone with their full UUID can read and copy them. Share the full UUID returned by this tool; legacy 8-character IDs only resolve within your own skills and the catalog. Only the owner may update, rename, or delete the original. Do not include private transcripts or credentials in reusable packages.

tools.name: manage_design_style
tools.description:
Manage saved Design Styles and the current project's visual identity. For concrete MG instances, use browse_library.

# Actions
- list: current active style and the user's saved styles.
- get: full designSpec, reviewed font pools, reference preview, related instances and nextReferenceSearch for the active style or a specified designStyleId. No active style is a normal result.
- create: a named user-owned style. Auto-applies by default; applyToProject:false saves without switching the project. Use for custom user identities; catalog selections use apply_preset.
- apply: select an existing saved style by designStyleId.
- update: patch spec, rename or set thumbnailUrl; targets the active style unless designStyleId is supplied. Editing a catalog preset forks a user-owned copy. Updating a style used by multiple projects requires the confirmation protocol below.
- clear: detach the active style without deleting it.
- delete: permanently remove a saved style after confirmation. Existing assets remain.

# Catalog presets
- list_presets: numbered visual collages and catalog UUIDs. Optional applicableLanguages (cjk/western), scenario, query, locale and limit/offset; locale only localizes text. Follow nextBrowse until complete within the requested scope. Summaries omit the full designSpec. Use returned names/thumbnailUrls with the host's supported style picker.
- apply_preset: select the existing catalog UUID from list_presets without creating a copy. For MG work, call `get` after applying to load the fresh full designSpec.

# Confirmation
When a response has status:"confirmation_required", relay its impact and ask the user. Retry only after confirmation with the specified flag: confirmShared:true for a shared update, confirm:true for delete. A separate variant can be created instead of changing a shared style.

# designSpec shape
Each array element's role describes its use, such as primary, heading or wordmark.

```json
{
  "colors": [{"role":"primary","value":"#6C5CE7"}],
  "fonts": [{"role":"heading","family":"Inter"}],
  "logos": [{"role":"wordmark","url":"https://..."}],
  "images": [{"role":"style reference","url":"https://..."}],
  "referenceSources": [{"id":"mg-reference:style:<UUID>"}],
  "styleGuide": "Editorial typography; heading weight 700."
}
```

- colors: hex value and usage role, with optional free-form palette label; fonts: default/applied CSS family and usage role, with optional language, weight, style, sourceUrl and review evidence (match, validation, notes).
- fontRecommendations: complete reviewed pools grouped by en / zh-Hans. These candidates do not replace the preset's default fonts.
- logos/images: URL and role identifying the variant/content/use.
- referenceSources: selected style or instance IDs recording visual identity sources. Cross-style form-only sources belong to individual MG calls, not this project identity.
- styleGuide: reusable confirmed tone, material and motion rules, plus typography details not represented by font entries (language, weight, italic, variable-font axes). Avoid duplicating palette/families or inventing one-off layouts and coordinates.

On update, colors merge by palette + role when palette is supplied. Without palette, a role must identify one color; repeated roles across palettes require specifying palette. Existing color metadata is preserved. Roles match case-insensitively after trimming; palette labels retain their exact identity. Fonts with language merge by language + role, otherwise retain legacy role/family matching (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized). fontRecommendations replaces the pool. Logos, images and referenceSources REPLACE their arrays: get first and include entries to retain. styleGuide replaces; an empty string clears it.

thumbnailUrl is the UI cover, not a generation reference. Save the same URL in designSpec.images only when it should also guide generation; referenceSources records provenance. Reference IDs do not populate image fields or deliver image bytes to the generator.

Style names are unique per user; collisions receive a numeric suffix automatically.

tools.description:
Preview one timeline through independently selectable views of its structure, composed viewer frames, and bounded transcript.

Views
- timeline: tracks and their state, placed items, gaps, layering references, effects and transitions (timeline frames, attached clips), and visible markers in the selected range.

Batch an overview or comparison in one call: 12-20 samples for a broad survey, then exact frames for small text or a change. Samples show only sampled moments, so inspect adjacent frames around entry/exit before judging a cut, fade, or motion. One labeled contact sheet returns inline (Desktop and the Web agent also save it at workspacePath), with exact times and FPS in the text.

tools.name: apply_script
tools.description:
Apply the edits already authored as `timeline.md` to the canonical timeline. This is the commit step for Script edits: it diffs the file against the live state and commits the core timeline change atomically (any core-row error rolls back the whole apply). After a successful apply, `timeline.md` is re-materialized clean (no `~~…~~`). Read it again only when starting another global semantic editing pass.

# Workflow

Pair with `read_script`: first call `read_script`, then edit the materialized `timeline.md`, then call this tool — using the same transport `read_script` established: workspace surfaces edit `timeline.md` in place and call `apply_script()` with no `timelineMd`; external surfaces edit the inline `timelineMd` string and pass the full edited content back via `apply_script({timelineMd: "<edited>"})`. For preview before commit, pass `preview: true`.

# Valid Script edits

The edit syntax — strike forms (`[s5] keep~~drop~~keep`), silence markers, the no-rewrite rule for `[sN]` rows, Chinese no-added-spaces — is defined in `read_script`; author edits exactly per that contract. Rules that matter at commit time:

- Author the whole arrangement (reorders, repeats, multiple versions back-to-back) and commit it in one apply.
- Occurrence anchors: moving or repeating an existing `[sN@M]` row preserves that explicitly chosen occurrence and its treatment; adding a bare library `[sN]` row creates a fresh play with source defaults. Preserve the `@N` suffix on the specific existing occurrence you edit, move, or delete; for hook replacement, remove only the copied hook occurrence rows, not the body occurrence.
- Matching is tolerant to case, punctuation, and accidental word-boundary whitespace (`and it` vs `andit`); it is NOT tolerant to changing the spoken words themselves. Use `manage_transcript` action `fix` when the transcript text is wrong.

# Expected timeline result

As documented in `read_script`: middle deletions/moves split clips around the kept ranges — more clips is expected physical editing, not a failure. Cover distracting jump cuts after the A-roll edit.

# Output

The successful result is a bounded summary. Preview retains positional and removed-row detail for inspection.

# Caveats

- This does not correct ASR mistakes. If the source transcript text itself is wrong, use `manage_transcript` action `fix` before editing Script.
- Do not simplify an existing `[sN@M]` row to `[sN]` while editing, moving, or deleting that occurrence; that selects source content instead of the authored occurrence. Keep the anchor when replaying its treatment; use a bare library row for defaults.
- Each `[sN]` line must be a contiguous substring of its source segment. Do NOT rewrite or fabricate words.
- Inline strikethrough is valid: `[s4] ~~uh, ~~improvements` deletes only `uh, ` and keeps `improvements`. Never expand a user-approved inline strike to a whole-line deletion.
- If the timeline was modified externally since the last `read_script`, apply refuses (stale state). Recovery: re-materialize via `read_script`, review the new state, then re-edit and re-apply.

tools.name: clean_script
tools.description:
Mechanical first-pass cleanup for talking-head transcripts already on the timeline: fixed filler-token removal plus batch silence pause compression / restoration. This call writes the canonical timeline immediately and has no preview parameter. For cleanup tasks where immediate application is intended, run this before semantic Script editing when fixed fillers or long pauses are present. Both capabilities run by default; use `only` to pick one. Runs incrementally — no-op if the bin asset isn't placed; per-item decoration and prior Script edits are preserved.

This is not a semantic speech editor. Anything that requires understanding meaning, tone, retakes, repeated ideas, or context-dependent verbal habits belongs in Script (`read_script` → `~~...~~` in `timeline.md` → `apply_script`).

If the user asks to preview the whole requested edit before it is applied, do not call `clean_script` first. Call `read_script({showSilence:true})`, stage the fixed-filler strikes, semantic edits, and pause edits together in `timeline.md`, then call `apply_script({preview:true})`. For pause compression, use the cross-surface rewrite syntax `[silence=Xs→Ys]` with the Unicode `→`; replacing it with a bare `[silence=Ys]` is not a compression rewrite on Web. When a struck filler has retained silence on both sides, deleting it joins those durations: a 250ms cap is their combined retained total, not 250ms per side. For example, left `0.48s→0.25s` plus an unchanged right `0.13s` yields `0.38s`; allocate the two sides to total `0.25s` instead of expecting the planner to infer a global cap. When preview succeeds and the user's request already authorizes application, call `apply_script` again without preview; do not ask for another confirmation. If the user asked only for a preview, stop without applying.

# Filler-word removal

Strikes only this fixed token list:
- EN: `um / uh / er / ah`
- ZH: `呃 / 额`

Ambiguous/contextual fillers and verbal habits are excluded: `呢 / 啊 / 嗯 / mm / hmm`, repeated phrases, stutters, retakes, and semantic repetition. If the user explicitly wants one of these heard words removed, delete it with Script, e.g. `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`.

# Pause / silence cleanup

Use the `silence` field to translate pause-editing requests directly — the four rule forms (`compress` / `restore` / `normalize` / `range`), the never-invents-silence guarantee, and legacy syntax are defined on the `silence` field. Quick request mapping: "tighter breaths" → default `compress:250`; "only compress long pauses over 0.8s" → `longSilence: 800`; "more breathing room, keep at least 0.5s" → `restore:500`.

Whole-track cleanup includes source padding before the first spoken word and after the final spoken word, including a recording tail left between the last word and stopping the camera. Do not leave that tail for a separate manual Script pass.

Internally this rewrites `[silence=Xs]` → `[silence=Xs→Ys]` and applies the result to the timeline.

You do not need to expose silence markers first. `timeline.md` may hide `[silence=Ns]` by default, but clean_script materializes the needed silence information internally and applies the batch rewrite.

# When NOT to use

Do not use this for precise user-specified word deletion, `呢` / `啊` / `嗯` cleanup, choosing the best retake, deleting duplicate sentences, fixing ASR mistakes, or any edit where the right answer depends on the sentence meaning. Use Script for playback edits and `manage_transcript` action `fix` for ASR correction.

After automatic cleanup, use the bounded result to continue. Read Script state only when starting semantic editing that requires transcript judgment.

Other forms: `"restore:500"` makes short pauses longer up to 500ms only when that pause was already that long in the original recording; `"normalize:500"` moves every editable pause toward 500ms; `"range:300-800"` keeps pauses between 300ms and 800ms; `"normalize:500,range:300-800"` changes only pauses whose current duration is 300–800ms, setting them toward 500ms while leaving shorter and longer pauses alone. Any rule that makes a pause longer never invents new silence; it only recovers pause time that already existed at that exact spot. Atomically add, update, or delete MemoryModel clips and treatments. Media types: audio, video, image, gif, svg, motion-graphic. Attached types: pixel-effect, pixel-transition, audio-effect, audio-transition. Adds require type + assetId or fromItemId; updates/deletes find entries by id; type is optional and must match if given. Updates cannot change a media item's type or assetId: replace media with a delete and add in the same call. Time fields and fades are frames; sourceIn is integer microseconds. validateOnly returns the complete plan without committing. Captions use edit_captions; transcript-driven cuts use read_script/apply_script.

Picture and sound are separate clips. Ordinary media edits use top-level includeLinked/includeGrouped, both default true. Media links and manual groups are independent. Set both false to target only named clips; these flags do not unlink or ungroup them. Sound-bearing video adds create linked picture/audio; copies create fresh links. media=audio inserts sound from a Video Asset alone. Sound-only adds require known audio. Unresolved combined videos retain their sound intent. Links may include external recordings and do not prove synchronization. Address the intended audio IDs for gain/fades; video-only pictures have no embedded audio.

Trim an edge with updates:[{id:"picture-id",trim:{edge:"start",atFrame:45}}]; edge is start or end. Linked edges move by the same delta, preserving J/L offsets and using each clip's own source clock. Trimming one component's edge with both relationship flags false creates a split edit while retaining source synchronization. Changing startFrame alone moves the clip without changing sourceIn and can shift its synchronization. Manual groups expand aligned edges. Source-bound or collision failures refuse the batch. trim cannot combine with startFrame, startDeltaFrames, durationFrames, sourceIn, playbackRate, or trackId; treatment fields may accompany it. Ordinary timing/source patches retain their combined-update behavior.

A media add without durationFrames uses the remaining source duration. fit:"cover"|"contain" derives crop from the full source frame, replacing existing crop. fadeInDurationFrames/fadeOutDurationFrames control audio volume or visual opacity; audioFadeInDurationFrames/audioFadeOutDurationFrames target embedded video audio. For audio/video gain, use one of volume/audioVolume (linear 0–1) or decibelAdjustment; muted:true silences it.

Whole-item pixel effects use targetItemId (any visual clip); block effects use trackId + startFrame + durationFrames and cannot overlap media or other blocks. Audio effects require exactly one targetItemId (audio/video), trackId, or target:"master", with no frame range.

Transitions use adjacent outgoingItemId + incomingItemId + durationFrames. Picture transitions include real linked Audio cuts at their own frames, including J/L cuts; explicit audio Assets default to audio only. Entry-level includeLinked:false targets only the named cut. Duration updates preserve cohort IDs and peer Assets. Exact centered durations refuse locked cuts or insufficient handles; validateOnly lists all planned IDs/types/durations. Cross Dissolve defaults to Cross Fade 0dB (builtin:transition-audio-constant-gain); builtin:transition-audio-cross-fade is equal-power.

Use typed keyframes for ordered atomic set/delete/move/curve/remove operations after reading inspect_item. They target only named owners and retain underlying static fields. X/Y, dimensions and crop edges are independent; animated audio values are absolute dB. Curve easing applies from its frame to the next point. Never replace all animation JSON to change one point. There is no json input or Web field aliases.

Desktop unified Mask uses assetId="builtin:effect-mask" with targetItemId or a ranged video track. Inspect that asset for tool definitions/defaults. adds and updates accept a typed mask:{mode:"set"|"coverage",nodes:[...],corrections:[...]}. Each tool needs a stable id, kind, enabled, invert, startFrame and durationFrames (half-open, relative to the effect), parameters; ordinary nodes also need operation:"intersect"|"union"|"subtract"|"xor". Effect-level propertyOverrides.transparency is 0..1, default 0: evaluation starts at alpha 1-transparency, then folds nodes in saved order; Union and hand painting can restore coverage above that starting alpha. Effect-level alphaProcessing is "none" (default), "premultiply", or "unpremultiply"; it changes completed RGB without changing alpha. Stroke outlines the completed Mask after all ordinary operations and hand corrections. Set effect-level propertyOverrides.outlineStyle ("none" default, "solid", or "dashed"), outlineColor, outlineWidth, outlinePlacement, outlineDashLength, outlineDashGap and outlineDashOffset; animate numeric/color stroke properties with properties.outline* paths; outlineStyle is static. No tool accepts outline* parameters, mask.<toolId>.outline* overrides or properties.mask.<toolId>.outline* animation. Keep hand tools in corrections only. A hand raster is immutable rg8-kb-rle data with width, height and a fresh revision; preserve untouched rasters. Replacing mask replaces the complete tool structure; preserve unmentioned tools and their IDs. Update tool parameter values using propertyOverrides keys mask.<toolId>.<parameter>, or animate properties.mask.<toolId>.<parameter> through keyframes. Effect-level transparency animation uses properties.transparency; alphaProcessing is static. Removing a tool removes its override and animation addresses. Track masks cannot contain portrait, smart or depth; each generated kind may occur only once even when disabled. Chroma channel is "rgb" (default), "luma", "red", "green", "blue", "hue", "saturation", or "lightness". RGB selects colors near color using threshold; other channels use inclusive channelMin/channelMax in 0..1, independently of the saved RGB color/threshold. tools.name: edit_captions
tools.description:
Edit the open local Project's canonical Memory caption model. For an ASR mistake, correct the source transcript with manage_transcript FIX before caption polishing. set_card_text changes only viewer-facing display wording or translation; it does not correct the source transcript.

Supported actions:
- batch: pass edits (not json), with 1–100 operations. Each edit is {"action":...} plus the same fields that action takes in json. Allowed actions: style, track, set_card_text, set_card_style, set_card_layout, split_card, merge_cards. Example: {"action":"batch","edits":[{"action":"set_card_text","cardId":"...","text":"Shorter display wording"},{"action":"set_card_style","cardId":"...","style":{"fontSize":64}}]}. Operations calculate in order against the current canonical caption model and commit once; an invalid operation writes nothing and returns CAPTION_BATCH_EDIT_FAILED with zero-based details.index and details.action. No nested batch, translation, preset-catalog reading, or source transcript changes. The final commit may regroup Cards after preset/style changes while preserving source-bound overrides. For precise per-Card edits, first apply baseline style, read the resulting Cards, then batch their refinements. A batch cannot reference new ids returned by an earlier operation.
- enable: show the caption item. When no caption item exists, or its caption model has zero tracks, initialize the default media sources using their existing word or sentence transcription. An existing item's identity, style and geometry are retained. Any existing caption tracks, including manual, imported, hidden or translated tracks, retain their Cards and individual visibility. Use track to restore a hidden original or translation. Plain is the default preset for creation.
- set_card_text: replace one Card's viewer-facing text, without correcting source transcription. Use manage_transcript FIX for an ASR error in the source, before polishing derived captions.
- set_card_style: merge or replace one Card's sparse style override. Pass {"cardId":"...","style":{...},"mode":"merge"|"replace"}; merge is the default. Replacement removes omitted Card overrides, so those fields inherit again.
- set_card_layout: merge or replace one Card's left/top/width/height override.
- split_card: pass {"cardId":"...","beforeTokenId":"..."} using words[].id returned by read_captions words=true for that Card.
- merge_cards: pass {"cardId":"..."} to merge a Card with the immediately following Card on its track, or {"cardIds":["...","..."]} to merge two or more adjacent Cards of one track into the earliest one.
- template: list the language-aware built-in caption presets, or apply one with templatePreset. This action does not bind generated MG templates.
- style: apply an optional built-in preset and then merge caption item style fields. Pass {"preset":"plain"} in json to select a preset; explicit style fields override that preset.
- track: pass exactly one selector. {"trackId":"<caption track id from read_captions>","visible":true} shows an existing caption track; visible:false hides it. trackId also accepts languageCode or style and switches between existing original, translated, and bilingual captions without retranslating. {"sourceTrackId":"<timeline source track id from read_captions coverage>","visible":true} binds or shows that source's ORIGINAL captions using its existing transcript; visible may be omitted. This creates missing word or sentence caption Cards without starting transcription or changing translations or other sources. With sourceTrackId, visible:false hides existing original caption tracks for that source; an unbound original stays unbound. Translation visibility, Cards and styles remain unchanged for both true and false, including when the source initially has only translated captions. Use trackId to address translations independently or change caption track language or style. Exact ids take precedence over unique prefixes. The same selectors work in structured batch track operations.
- translate: translate existing source captions into a separate language track. Pass {"languageCode":"es"} in json; mode defaults to "bilingual" (shows both source and translation), or use "translation" to show only the translation. For bilingual, primary "original" or "translation" puts that language on top. Optional trackId selects a source caption track or its source media track by id/prefix; omit it to translate visible source tracks and sources with a visible translation in the target language. Enable captions first if none exist. Use this action for subtitle translation; set_card_text is for individual wording edits.
- disable: hide captions while preserving their Cards and styles. Source transcription and source clip edits update derived caption tracks automatically, including while hidden.

For a simple add-captions request, enable Plain directly. Apply explicitly requested style edits directly. If the user asks to see, compare, or choose styles, load widget-forms and show native caption preset or Desktop custom-style candidates before editing; do not add a mandatory chooser to other requests. Custom candidates use caption-style-id/name/caption-style JSON with optional caption-base-preset-id. Previewing does not mutate the timeline or save a preset. After submission, use the exact normalized Memory settings and recorded target/application call from the hidden selection context. Custom preview fields are a supported ordinary-caption subset; arbitrary CSS and generated templates are separate workflows. Optional json.timelineId guards selection application: if it no longer matches the active timeline, no caption edit is committed. Template application also accepts json.captionsItemId to guard the captured item.

When the user asks to restore/show existing original or bilingual captions, read_captions lists all tracks including hidden ones and provides a showAction for each hidden track. Pass that showAction to edit_captions. Do not use translate as a visibility workaround, invent a target language, or generate a temporary translation and then hide it. Use translate only when the user requests creating or updating a translation in that language.

Progressive word reveal is a shared native style rule: use style.reveal {"mode":"progressive","unit":"word"} with style, track or set_card_style. It reveals each word at its existing timestamp and retains it until the current Card/page ends, reserving layout space for future words. Use {"mode":"all","unit":"word"} to show the whole phrase together again. This is independent of highlightUnit and displayMode; do not substitute highlighting, pacing:"word", wordsPerPage:1, or one-word Cards for a request to reveal words within natural phrases. Reveal does not add bounce/fade animation. Word timing must already exist; words sharing a timestamp appear together. Apply the rule once, not to every token. Templates own their drawing but receive reveal-aware caption.words[].visible. Verify before and after word onset with preview_timeline.

Native v8 stores current-word emphasis in activeToken: {"color":"#ffff00","background":null,"animation":{...}}. Flat highlightColor/highlightBackground are not accepted. token.animation controls how words enter/exit; activeToken.animation runs when spoken emphasis is active. Example style: {"reveal":{"mode":"progressive","unit":"word"},"token":{"animation":{"enter":{"durationMs":180,"easing":"ease-out","keyframes":[{"offset":0,"opacity":0,"transform":{"translateY":"0.25em","scale":0.9}},{"offset":1,"opacity":1,"transform":{"translateY":"0em","scale":1}}]}}}}. One shared rule applies to every word. Without progressive reveal, token entry starts when its Card/page appears. Animation phases enter/exit use durationMs (1–2000), easing, and 2–8 keyframes with increasing offsets from 0 to 1. Supported properties: opacity, transform (scale, rotate in degrees, translateX/translateY in px or em), clipPath (inset). Set animation:null to disable inherited animation. Slot members inherit independently; background and animation are replaced atomically. stackedActiveStyle is only static color/background for the existing stacked highlighted-row behavior; it is not a cue animation.


Generated caption templates use the native style.template field in style, track, or set_card_style: {"template":{"path":"<absolute local source entry path>","runtime":"remotion","properties":{...}}}. runtime is "remotion" or "html"; properties is optional. For example, set_card_style json may be {"cardId":"...","style":{"template":{"path":"/project/.agent-workspace/caption.jsx","runtime":"remotion"}}}. Use an absolute local entry path, preferably inside a project-owned persistent location. The template directly references the entry without copying or registering it in the asset library; do not call push_asset for a caption template. Template inheritance follows caption item -> track -> Card. template:null explicitly stops inheritance and renders ordinary captions. Omitting template in a merge preserves the existing override; removing the override restores inheritance (for a Card, replace its style with the intended remaining fields and omit template). Successfully saving the reference does not prove it renders actual caption content: inspect the bound Cards on the timeline.

Card and token start/end values returned by read_captions are integer microseconds. Its atFrame/fromFrame/toFrame queries use frames; convert using the project frame rate before frame-based operations. Do source transcript and clip changes before final Card edits: affected derived tracks rebuild when their source changes.

Each action rejects json fields it does not read and lists the ones it accepts; revision is accepted and ignored. Edits use the latest MemoryProjectModel state and autosave to the local Project file.

tools.name: read_script
tools.description:
Script edits spoken content as text, deriving source ranges from accepted transcript word timings and applying the arrangement atomically with stale-state protection. For read-only source transcript excerpts or source frames, use `inspect_asset` instead.

This tool materializes the current cut for one speech track (`timeline.md`) and full source transcripts (`library/<filename>.md`). By default it picks the first timeline track containing transcribed media; pass `track` to select a different speech track explicitly. On surfaces with a workspace filesystem (ChatCut backend agent with a sandbox attached), the files appear on disk; read and edit them with `read_workspace_file` / `edit_workspace_file` / `write_workspace_file` in Codex plugin sessions, or the equivalent native `Read` / `Edit` / `Write` tools. On external surfaces without a workspace, `timeline.md` and the library docs are returned inline in the tool result; edit the `timelineMd` string with your own tools, then pass the full edited content back via `apply_script({timelineMd})`.

# When to use

Use this for any operation that uses transcript text or meaning to decide what plays:
- Delete a spoken word / filler / context-dependent verbal habit, e.g. `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`
- Delete or compress a visible silence marker / breath pause
- Trim, restore, move, copy, reorder, or delete transcript segments
- Choose the best retake and remove failed attempts or semantic duplicates
- Make clips / highlights / a short version / several versions based on what the speaker says, e.g. "cut slices", "keep the part about pricing", "make a 30s version", "make three versions on one track", "remove the intro"
- Pull library transcript onto the timeline, including an initial transcript-driven cut

# When NOT to use

Not for: correcting ASR mistakes in the source transcript (`manage_transcript` action `fix`); non-transcript media or visual properties (B-roll / MG / overlays / effects / transitions / position changes, use `edit_item`); mechanical whole-track filler cleanup or batch silence compression/restoration (`clean_script`); timestamp lookup for placing non-transcript objects (`find_transcript`); asset library browsing (`browse_assets`).

Script preserves transcript word boundaries and occurrence identity during text edits. Bare library rows create fresh placements with default treatment. Repeating an existing anchored row preserves the explicitly chosen occurrence's treatment, media links and attached effects; ordinary clip copies do the same. Native tools also support editing only its picture or sound; frame-based splits use the timeline frame grid.

# Workspace files

- `timeline.md`: the current cut for the selected speech track. Structure:
  - `## V1` / `## A2`: H2 track section (alias from track type + order).
  - `### IMG_4560.mp4`: H3 source region (6-hex `[shortId]` suffix on filename collision). **Preserve H3 text exactly**; apply maps H3 to asset by it.
  - Body rows under each H3:
    - `[sN] text`: playing transcript segment (source-local id; only re-transcription changes it). Timeline rows render as `[sN@1]`, `[sN@2]`, etc., identifying each current occurrence; preserve the suffix when editing, moving or deleting it. Repeat the anchored row to replay its treatment. A bare library `[sN]` row selects source content with default treatment.
    - `[cN] Nf`: non-transcript clip from this source (frame duration).
    - `[gap Nf]`: empty timeline space between items on this track (no source playing). On the only visible video track, this renders as black video.
    - `@speakerName`: render-only speaker boundary (auto-derived on re-materialize; no need to maintain when reordering or copying lines).
    - `[silence=Ns]`: inter-word or inter-segment silence. **Appears only when `showSilence: true`**; by default the file renders without these markers.
  Body order on disk = playback order.

- `library/<filename>.md`: full source transcript per transcribed asset. Library files are NOT valid `timeline.md` files: they use `# filename` H1 headers and source-local rows only. To bring content on-timeline, preserve `timeline.md`'s top markers, keep/create a `## V1` track section plus `### <filename>` source regions, then copy `[sN]` rows from `library/*.md` under the matching `###` region. Do not paste or concatenate whole library files into `timeline.md`.

# Editing workflow

Edit loop: first call materializes the files (clean, no `~~…~~`) → read `timeline.md` (workspace tools, or the inline content returned by this tool on external surfaces) → edit `timeline.md` with `Edit` (put multiple replacements in one `edits` array so they preflight and validate together; if rewriting, preserve the top `# Timeline`, `script-stamp`, `script-timeline`, `script-track`, and `<!-- script:body -->` markers). Validation runs after each filesystem edit. If diagnostics are returned, the changed file remains current: read it and fix forward with Edit. Only after validation passes, immediately call `apply_script()` (workspace-backed surface) or `apply_script({timelineMd: "<edited>"})` (external) before starting another global semantic pass. Apply re-materializes `timeline.md` clean; just read it again. Reuse it while its scope and revision remain valid. Re-call this tool after a stale-script error, a timeline/track scope change, or to change `showSilence`; set `refreshCache: true` when the source transcript changed. Reapply your intended edits to the refreshed script; do not overwrite its revision markers with old ones.

Track scope: omit `track` for normal transcript editing; the tool picks the default speech track. Keep the track section returned in `timeline.md`. To choose another speech track, use its existing alias/id from the timeline rather than assuming V1 or A1.

# How to edit `timeline.md`

Strike (`~~…~~`) marks source content to remove from playback:

  Drop words in a segment        [s5] keep ~~drop~~ keep
  Drop Chinese particle          [s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月
  Drop a whole row               delete the line, OR wrap it:
                                   ~~[s5] hello world~~
                                   ~~[c1] 30f~~
                                   ~~[gap 30f]~~
  Keep only the start/end        trim text from the beginning or end of a row
  Disambiguate text repeats      [s5] ~~anchor~~ wanted
  Reorder / move a row           move the line on disk in any order; apply re-derives all frames
  Replay / repeat a row          repeat an anchored [sN@M] row to copy its treatment, or add bare [sN] from the library for source defaults; each is a separate play of that content. Sequence whole versions back-to-back on one track by repeating rows (Script derives the timing).

Every `~~...~~` pair must open and close on the same physical line. To drop consecutive rows, delete them or wrap each row separately; never open `~~` before one `[sN]` row and close it after a later row.

`[sN]` rows edit words that were actually spoken in the source. Do not rewrite the wording or add words the source never said. If you need to remove words from the middle of a row, keep the row text and wrap only the unwanted source text in `~~...~~`; do not skip over the middle words by rewriting the row.

For Chinese text, do not add spaces that are not in the source:
- Correct: `[s1] 过去~~呢~~一个月`
- Wrong: `[s1] 过去一个月` (skips the middle word without marking it)
- Wrong: `[s1] 过去 ~~呢~~ 一个月` (adds spaces the source does not contain)

# Expected timeline result

Script edits rebuild timeline clips from source ranges. If you only trim the start or end of a clip, the result may stay as one trimmed clip. If you delete or move content from the middle of a clip, the original continuous source range cannot remain one clip: apply will create new clips for the kept ranges before and after the removed/moved range.

Predict the clip structure before applying: each middle deletion or middle move creates additional clip boundaries. This is expected physical editing, not a failed or unsupported word deletion. Still perform the requested spoken-content edit when the user asks for it; if the new clip boundaries create visible jump cuts, handle them afterward with optional B-roll / visual cover.

Do not create a bare `[gap]` on the primary video track to add breathing room. For pacing, preserve or restore source silence with `[silence=...]` / `clean_script`; for visual transitions, cover the moment with B-roll, MG, a card, or another visible layer. A bare video-track gap is a black frame.

**View or cut a specific breath / pause (剪气口)**: pass `showSilence: true` only when you need to inspect or manually adjust a specific pause. Strike `~~[silence=0.8s]~~` to cut it, or rewrite `[silence=0.8s→0.2s]` to compress it. For batch silence adjustment across the track (compress or restore), use `clean_script`; hidden silence markers do not prevent clean_script from processing them internally.

# User-facing language

You MUST NOT explain edits to the user with internal addresses such as `[sN]`, `[cN]`, `[gap]`, word indices, clip ids, or segment ids. The user cannot see those addresses and will not understand what they mean. Use them only in thinking, file edits, and tool calls. In chat, describe edits with the actual spoken content, a short quote, or a plain-language description.

tools.name: get_css_styles
tools.description:
Retrieve matched CSS rules, inline styles (element.style), inherited styles, custom properties, and cascade wrappers (@layer, @media, @container, @scope) for an element identified by its UID.
Rules are ordered from highest to lowest cascade precedence and include source line numbers (e.g. index:196). Active (winning) declarations have no prefix tag, while (losing) overridden declarations are prefixed with [overloaded].
Treat the output as authoritative and complete.
Results are paginated (10 rules per page by default); use pageIdx to page through the remaining rules. Requires a UID from take_snapshot.

tools.name: js
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in a persistent `node_repl` with top-level await. Top-level bindings persist until `js_reset` and can be redeclared. Use `const` for stable values and `let` for changing values. Use dynamic imports such as `await import("playwright")`; top-level static imports and `node:process` are unavailable. Use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for output and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. Execution context is available through `nodeRepl.cwd`, `nodeRepl.homeDir`, `nodeRepl.tmpDir`, and `nodeRepl.requestMeta`. The default timeout is 30000 ms (30 seconds); increase `timeout_ms` for longer operations. Use `js_add_node_module_dir` when an additional package directory is required.
